children: Household appliance maker Whirlpool Corp. continues to battle declining sales and shrinking margins, slashing its full-year guidance as it reports a slower than expected recovery.
The stock tumbled 8.5% in late Monday trading, after closing down 5.9%, at $26.44, in regular trading.
For the third quarter ended in September, Whirlpool reported an adjusted loss of 21 cents a share on revenue of $3.68 billion. Net sales were down 8.8% from a year ago.

CEO Marc Bitzer said the company was taking out structural costs and raising prices, which has driven progress on margins. "While the pace of recovery is slower than expected, these actions are setting a clear path for further improvements in 2027," he said.
Wall Street was expecting adjusted earnings of 73 cents a share on sales of $3.93 billion.
The ongoing earnings before interest and taxes margin was 2.6% in the third quarter, compared with 4.5% in the third quarter last year.

Of that quarterly revenue, Whirlpool reported major domestic appliance sales of $2.495 billion in North America, down 8.3% and below expectations for $2.72 billion. Sales of major appliances in Latin America increased 6.9% to $858 million, above the $852 million projected. Global sales of small domestic appliances fell 0.7% to $286 million.

Whirlpool reported negative $1.08 billion in free cash flow for the quarter, larger than the $907 million negative free cash flow in the previous third quarter, whereas analysts were expecting free cash flow of $124 million.

Chief Financial Officer Roxanne Warner said in the same statement that "Through disciplined working capital management, we are protecting our year end free cash flow and our balance sheet resilience to navigate challenging market conditions. As a result, we now expect net debt below $4.5 billion at the end of 2026 and have preserved a clear debt maturity ladder until 2028."

Whirlpool lowered its full-year revenue guidance to about $14.5 billion, from about $15 billion in the previous quarter, which had been lowered from $15.5 billion previously. It now expects a loss of $1.30 a share, down from its previous guidance for $2.50 to $3.00 in the previous quarter.
Nevertheless, it still expects free cash flow of about $300 million for the full year, which had been reduced from about $450 million previously.
Whirlpool management will host a conference call to discuss its financial results at 8 a.m. Eastern time on Tuesday.
On May 6, Whirlpool reported a loss of 56 cents a share from first-quarter sales of $3.3 billion. Analysts had expected earnings of 38 cents a share on sales of $3.4 billion, according to FactSet.
It also suspended its dividend, which had been 90 cents a quarter.

The Benton Harbor, Mich.-based manufacturer of kitchen and laundry appliances, whose brands include Whirlpool, KitchenAid, JennAir, Maytag, and Amana, has been battered by economic and policy uncertainty, rising costs, and aggressive competition.

The Supreme Court's February ruling overturning President Donald Trump's broad-based trade tariffs, which had helped Whirlpool compete against imported foreign appliances, now enabled those rivals to offer more competitive prices, Whirlpool said at the time. About 80% of the company's sales come from the U.S.
